projectName: Suite Identity: Tailnet Sign-In and Passkey Step-Up
description: Replace per-app passphrases, PINs, and name pickers with one household identity. The tailnet login (asserted by Tailscale Serve) identifies the member on every request with zero interaction. Home Base keeps the household directory and runs a suite passkey service that sensitive apps use for step-up checks. Sensitive apps and Home Base admin each get their own hostname so a compromised sibling app cannot drive them from the browser. Every app keeps its existing local auth as the standalone fallback.

timing.plannedEarliestExecution: After the Feature-4 Serve publishing lane is stable on production hosts
timing.gatingCondition: Spikes 1 and 2 passed on a test VM on 2026-10-23; spike 3 passed on 2026-10-25 (evidence.spike3) on Tailscale 1.102.4, except the second-tagged-host takeover check, which moves to the SID-008 rehearsal. Each production host must run Tailscale ≥ 1.102.4 and have its Serve topology confirmed read-only before SID-001 executes there.

principles: The tailnet login is the person, but only for logins the administrator has admitted to the directory. Tagged devices, unknown logins, and externally shared users get no identity
Members who never had a password get no new friction; apps that had passphrases trade them for nothing (tailnet-only) or a passkey tap (sensitive apps)
Identity headers are trusted only when the only possible path to the app is Tailscale Serve → a root-only nginx socket for that hostname → the app's own socket
The tailnet identity is ambient, like a cookie: every mutating request needs an exact Origin match and a JSON content type, and authorization runs before any mutation or step-up prompt
One hostname per trust boundary: low-friction apps share the suite hostname; each sensitive app and Home Base admin gets its own
Passkey checks never request the PRF extension; they prove presence only, so synced passkeys from third-party providers work on iOS
Classify credentials from what the authenticator proves: only a credential with verified attestation from a pinned hardware vendor root counts as a hardware key
The administrator is a Home Base designation, not an app role; apps keep parent/kid
Every app can still run standalone with its existing local auth
No acting as another member; no shared-device mode
Prefer the simplest storage: directory in Home Base state, a snapshot file Home Base owns and apps can only read (integrity from file ownership, not signatures)

decisions.D1: Tailnet identity is the suite identity, keyed on the tailnet's stable user ID. nginx resolves it on every request with auth_request to a Home Base identity endpoint (whois on Serve's client IP) and passes it as X-Sovereign-User-Id; the whois login must equal Tailscale-User-Login. If the lookup fails or disagrees, the request carries no identity (fail closed). The login string is display only
decisions.D2: No shared devices; tagged devices get no identity. Hosts that serve the suite must be tagged; the planner refuses tailnet mode on a user-owned node, where local processes would arrive as the node's owner
decisions.D3: No impersonation; a parent who needs a kid's view uses the kid's device
decisions.D4: Passkey checks only in sensitive apps (finance, estate documents, trading, Bitcoin accounting); previously passwordless apps get no new friction
decisions.D5: Multi-host federation deferred; each host is its own household instance keyed on tailnet identities
decisions.D7: Kid views in sensitive apps stay at tailnet level where the app already scopes kid data server-side
decisions.D8: Home Base admin requires a passkey: 8h session plus an every-time attested hardware key for privileged plans and administrator actions; the admin passphrase is used only in the setup and recovery states (D16)
decisions.D9: Operator apps (trading, Bitcoin accounting) use a 24h passkey session window
decisions.D10: 'administrator' is a Home Base-only flag, separate from parent; only an administrator can grant it; never synced between hosts
decisions.D11: Multiple credentials per member (synced passkeys and hardware keys side by side); the administrator must hold ≥2 credentials including ≥1 attested hardware key, and Home Base refuses (transactionally) to remove the last one
decisions.D12: One assurance policy matrix (assurancePolicy below) defines every protected action's level and credential kind; apps and Home Base enforce it through the shared library, not ad hoc
decisions.D13: The shared library and passkey code live in a new public repo, sovereignAuth, Node package at the root. Apps take it as a git dependency pinned to a commit (package-lock.json). A Python package under python/ is added when the first Python app migrates (wave 3), and must pass the same conformance vectors. Hosts need no GitHub credentials
decisions.D14: Separate hostnames via Tailscale Services, qualified by household instance: svc:<instance>-home (low-friction apps), svc:<instance>-homebase (admin), svc:<instance>-<app> per sensitive app. Each service has exactly one host; Home Base refuses to publish a service another host already advertises. Each service targets its own root-only nginx socket and serves only its own allowlisted mounts
decisions.D15: Credential kinds: synced, device-bound, hardware. 'hardware' requires attestation verified against pinned vendor root certificates shipped in sovereignAuth; flags alone never make a credential hardware
decisions.D16: Bootstrap states: setup → active → recovery (SID-004). Recovery is the only exception to the credential rules: the recorded administrator (same stable user ID) plus the passphrase may enroll replacement administrator credentials without an existing hardware check. Recovery ends when the administrator again meets D11 and completes a fresh hardware ceremony
decisions.D17: The RP ID is the tailnet domain, fixed when the first credential is enrolled. Because every hostname in the tailnet can start a ceremony for that RP ID, each ceremony accepts exactly one origin: https://<the hostname it was served on> (port 443 only), and the cookie or token it produces is scoped to that hostname. Home Base serves ceremonies only on hostnames it publishes. The RP ID is not configurable per host. The only change is a tailnet rename, which rebinds it, orphans every credential, bumps the global epoch, and enters recovery (runbook section 7)
decisions.D18: Snapshot trust comes from file ownership: Home Base writes it into a directory it owns that apps can read but not write. Apps open it by descriptor (no symlinks) and refuse it unless the file and directory are owned by the Home Base user and writable by no one else. It is rewritten on every change and every 30 s; apps re-check at most every 5 s and refuse it when older than 120 s
decisions.D19: Token redemption goes over a per-app Home Base socket, /run/sovereign-identity/<app>.sock (owner Home Base user, group the app's user, 0660), so the socket path authenticates the calling app. Redemption fails closed on timeout or Home Base restart
decisions.D20: All service hostnames in one tailnet are a single browser site: ts.net is a public suffix, so <service>.<tailnet>.ts.net names are same-site to each other (spike 3: Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site; a Domain=<tailnet>.ts.net cookie set on one hostname is sent to the others, even with SameSite=Strict). SameSite gives no isolation between them. Isolation therefore rests on: exact-Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin checks on mutations, __Host- prefixed cookies (which a sibling cannot set), aud-bound signed cookies, side-effect-free GET/HEAD, and refusing non-navigation requests from same-site or cross-site in sensitive apps and Home Base admin

levels.tailnet: An admitted member's identity headers on the request; no cookie needed
levels.session: An assurance cookie for this hostname within the app's window, with the member's current epoch and the household's current global epoch
levels.recent: An assurance cookie whose auth_time is ≤5 minutes old
levels.every-time: A single-use action token from a fresh ceremony, bound to this exact request

matrix.action: Use a low-friction app (dinner, fasting, help desk, calendar)
Link external accounts, export data, change a member's parent/kid role
A member adds or removes their own credential
matrix.kind: any (or an enrollment grant for a member with no credentials)

matrix.action: Administrator adds or removes an administrator credential
Privileged Home Base plans (install, repair, adopt, update, uninstall, restore), config changes, publishing changes, rotating secrets

evidence.spike1: Serve adds Tailscale-User-Login/Name and replaces client-forged copies; correct identity from macOS, iOS web wrapper, and a kid's Windows PC; tagged host gets no identity headers. nginx on a 0700 root unix socket refuses non-root local users. Found: nginx on 0.0.0.0 blocks Serve's tailnet :443 bind; apps bind 0.0.0.0 despite catalog upstreamBind; forged X-Sovereign-* passes unless nginx overwrites it; absolute redirects leak http://localhost behind the socket
evidence.spike2: Passkey enroll/step-up with 1Password (desktop and iPhone), Apple Passwords, and a USB-C YubiKey; tailnet-level RP ID accepted by Chrome and Safari; signed assurance cookie rejected on identity mismatch or tamper; single-use action tokens reject reuse, wrong action, wrong kind, wrong member, and expiry (in-memory, single process only); a non-administrator member enrolled a synced passkey, passed session and recent checks, and was refused the administrator action with 403 before any prompt. Limits: hardware classification came from flags (not proof; see D15); parent/kid roles not exercised; one origin only. Found: apps on loopback TCP can be reached directly with forged headers; all apps share one service user
spike3Required: Serve identity headers arrive on Tailscale Services (layer-7) traffic, as they do on node-level Serve
Two instance-qualified services on one host, each Serve config targeting its own nginx socket; each block serves only its allowlisted mounts and refuses the others
Serve's X-Forwarded-For when the client sends its own: confirm Serve overwrites it or appends, and that nginx takes only the Serve-added address
nginx auth_request to a Home Base whois endpoint over a unix socket returns the stable user ID; a tagged client returns none
A local process on the serving host requesting its own public service URL gets no member identity (tagged host); on a user-owned node, confirm it arrives as the owner (why D2 refuses that topology)
A second host cannot advertise the first host's instance-qualified service while Home Base's guard is in place

A YubiKey registration with attestation 'direct' verifies against the pinned vendor root; a software authenticator reporting the same flags, a self-attested credential, and a valid chain to an unpinned root do not
A page on the home service cannot read responses from a sensitive service, and its credentialed cross-origin POST is refused by the Origin check
evidence.spike3: Test VM, Tailscale 1.102.4, 2026-10-25, host tagged, two instance-qualified test services. Passed: Serve identity headers and unix-socket targets work on Tailscale Services; each service reaches only its own nginx socket and allowlisted mounts (others 404; a hostname sent to the other service's address gets 421); Serve overwrites client-sent X-Forwarded-For (single and multiple values) and X-Forwarded-Host; the nginx auth_request whois lookup returns the stable user ID and ignores forged X-Sovereign-*, Tailscale-User-*, X-Forwarded-* headers; stopping the identity endpoint fails requests closed; a non-root local user cannot connect to the nginx sockets. On the user-owned node, any local process (even nobody) reached the host's own Serve URL as the owner (confirms D2; a self-IP guard in the identity endpoint refused it); once tagged, local requests carry no login. A user-owned node is refused as a service host ("service hosts must be tagged nodes"). A YubiKey packed attestation verified against the pinned Yubico U2F root and was rejected with a wrong root; with no roots loaded the library skips chain checks (why SID-005 refuses that); a software authenticator's direct attestation was rejected under pinned roots and its none-attestation credential classified device-bound, where the spike-2 flag rule would have said hardware. Cross-hostname from the home service to a sensitive one: credentialed reads are blocked by CORS, a JSON POST stops at the preflight, a form POST reaches the app with the member's identity, Origin of the sibling, and Sec-Fetch-Site: same-site (refused by the SID-003 mutation guard). Found: hostnames are same-site (D20) and cookie tossing works; each new service hostname takes 35–40 s on first request while its certificate is issued; a service host cannot resolve its own service names through tailnet DNS. Not tested: a second tagged host trying to take over a service (SID-008)

userStories.title: Identity-safe ingress: per-service Serve → root-only nginx sockets
acceptanceCriteria: Both deployment paths change together: the publish planner and the root executor (executor/handlers.js nginx rendering) emit the same layout; a later install, repair, or update never reintroduces a TCP listener

Each published service (svc:<instance>-home, svc:<instance>-homebase, one svc:<instance>-<app> per sensitive app) targets its own socket /run/sovereign-serve/<service>.sock; the directory is created at boot by tmpfiles.d, 0700 root:root

The publisher checks endpoint conflicts per service (tcp:443 on a different service is not a conflict), verifies each service is advertised and approved for this host only, and refuses to publish a service another host already serves

Each server block includes only its own service's mounts (sovereign-home.d/<service>/), plus /_sovereign/auth/; admin routes exist only on the homebase service; a request whose X-Forwarded-Host doesn't match the block's hostname gets 421
Each nginx server block listens only on its socket (no TCP 80/443 for the suite), sets absolute_redirect off, and gives every mount an explicit 'location = /mount { return 301 /mount/; }'

A shared identity snippet is included inside every proxy location (nginx drops inherited proxy_set_header once a location sets its own). It runs auth_request to the Home Base identity endpoint (D1) and sets X-Sovereign-User-Id, X-Sovereign-Login, and X-Sovereign-Name from its answer and Serve's Tailscale-User-* headers, always overwriting client copies (absent ⇒ omitted); Host comes from X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto from Serve

Apps and Home Base read identity only from X-Sovereign-*; a forged X-Sovereign-* or Tailscale-User-* header is replaced or dropped on every location, including sidecar routes (e.g. the bug tracker's MCP location)
Planner refuses tailnet identity for an app whose upstream is still TCP, and on a user-owned (untagged) serving node; it says why

Feature-4 verification replaces the 'nginx listener on tcp:443' check with 'nginx sockets present, root-only, and each service targets its own'; readiness checks in src/operations/policy.js no longer assume ports

Rollback is dependency-ordered: the planner refuses to restore any TCP ingress while any app is in tailnet mode; the rollback plan first returns every app to local mode, then restores the saved Serve and nginx config
Publishing a service waits until its certificate is issued (first request takes 35–40 s) and verifies the hostname answers before any app on it switches to tailnet mode
The identity endpoint refuses lookups for the host's own tailnet addresses, as a backstop to D2
userStories.testStrategy: Planner, publisher, and executor rendering tests (snippet in every location, per-service allowlists, per-service conflict detection); VM rehearsal of the spike-1 and spike-3 checks per hostname: every mount requested on every other hostname is refused; forged and missing headers on every route; forged X-Forwarded-For; local bypass refused; local process against the public URL; tagged host no identity; redirects stay on the hostname

userStories.title: App listen contract and per-app ownership
acceptanceCriteria: Catalog gains a listen contract (runtime.listen = unix) and renders SOVEREIGN_LISTEN=unix:/run/sovereign-apps/<id>/app.sock; apps not yet supporting it render HOST=127.0.0.1 and stay in local mode
Socket directory /run/sovereign-apps/<id>: owner = the app's service user, group = nginx's group, mode 2750; socket 0660; recreated on restart. App service users are never members of nginx's group

Sensitive apps run as their own service user, and the whole ownership graph moves with them: checkout and its parent path (root-owned 0755 parents), code, .env, storage, backups, dependency installs and caches, timers and workers. The shared service user cannot write, replace, or read any of them
The executor installs dependencies and runs migrations as the app's own user, writes .env as root with the app's user as owner (0600), and stores that app's backups 0700 under its user

nginx upstreams keep each app's URI behavior: mount-preserving apps (trading, Bitcoin accounting) use 'proxy_pass http://unix:<sock>;' (no URI), prefix-stripping apps use 'proxy_pass http://unix:<sock>:/;'
Health checks and post-install verification work over the socket
userStories.testStrategy: Install-planner and executor tests for env/unit/nginx/ownership rendering; VM checks: the shared service user is refused by a sensitive app's socket and cannot read or write its checkout, .env, or backups; nested APIs, redirects, static assets, and OAuth callbacks work for one mount-preserving and one prefix-stripping app

userStories.title: sovereignAuth core library and wire contract
acceptanceCriteria: The sovereignAuth repo exists (public, Node package at the root, tagged releases) and is installed as a commit-pinned git dependency; a Home Base install on the VM succeeds without GitHub credentials
Defines and documents the wire contract: X-Sovereign-* headers, snapshot format, assurance cookie, action token, step-up 401 body

Snapshot reader (D18): opens by descriptor without following symlinks; refuses a snapshot that is missing, not owned by the Home Base user, writable by anyone else, older than 120 s, or of a lower generation than the last one seen; re-checks at most every 5 s

Request guard: the member comes from X-Sovereign-User-Id looked up in the snapshot (never from the login alone), and the snapshot's login for that ID must match X-Sovereign-Login; unknown, disabled, or tagged ⇒ no member; app modes are 'local' or 'tailnet' only, anything else fails closed; tailnet mode refuses to start unless listening on its socket

Mutation guard (default on for every non-GET/HEAD): Origin must equal this hostname's origin (same-site is not enough, D20), content type must be application/json, Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin when present. GET and HEAD handlers must have no side effects (a sibling hostname's GET reaches the app with the member's identity); exports and other actions are POST
Resource isolation (on by default for sensitive apps and Home Base admin): refuse a request whose Sec-Fetch-Site is same-site or cross-site unless it is a top-level GET navigation

requireAssurance(policyKey, {target}) reads the level and kind from the assurance policy matrix and returns step_up_required before the handler runs. Only the __Host-sv_assurance cookie is read (any other name, including a same-named cookie without the prefix, is ignored); it must match aud (this hostname), the member's epoch, and the global epoch. Every-time actions redeem the token over the app's own redemption socket (D19), passing the action and the target the app resolved before the 401, and Home Base rechecks the member's current authorization
Conformance vectors (valid, expired, wrong aud, stale epoch, replayed, wrong digest, unprefixed or tossed cookie, same-site Origin) ship with the repo for any later language port
The WebAuthn helpers extracted from the estate-documents app live here (D11)
userStories.testStrategy: Library unit tests driven by the conformance vectors; mutation-guard tests for cross-site form posts (text/plain), wrong Origin, and missing Origin

userStories.title: Household directory, bootstrap, and recovery
acceptanceCriteria: Directory records per member: suite_member_id, display name, tailnet stable user ID (required; from the per-request identity lookup, D1), current login, role parent|kid, administrator flag, status, credential epoch, per-app access (default all; operator apps default administrator-only). Logins and user IDs are unique
A request whose login matches a member but whose stable user ID does not is treated as unknown; administrator rights never follow a login string to a new account

Bootstrap state machine: 'setup' (no administrator credentials) → 'active' (≥2 administrator credentials including ≥1 attested hardware key) → 'recovery' (entered only by the passphrase while active, or by the root CLI)

In 'setup', the passphrase plus the founder's tailnet identity records that identity as the first administrator and allows only enrolling administrator credentials and editing the directory; no privileged plans

In 'active', the passphrase opens recovery only for the recorded administrator's stable user ID. Recovery permits exactly: enrolling replacement administrator credentials without an existing hardware check (the D16 exception) and revoking credentials. Entering recovery bumps the global epoch (every assurance cookie stops working), revokes sessions, challenges, frozen plans, and outstanding tokens, publishes the snapshot, and is audited

Recovery → active only when the administrator again meets D11 and completes a fresh ceremony with an attested hardware key; until then no privileged plan, config change, or administrator grant is possible

'homebase admin reset' (root shell) revokes all administrator credentials and sessions, bumps the global epoch, sets a new passphrase, and returns to 'setup'; '--administrator <login>' records a different tailnet account as administrator when the old one is gone; audited

Every enrollment by a member with no usable credentials (none, or only orphaned or demoted ones) needs an enrollment grant: single-use, issued by the administrator for that member, expires in 15 minutes

Home Base writes the snapshot (generation, written_at, global epoch, cookie-verification public keys, members, roles, epochs, app access; no credentials) per D18 on every change and every 30 s; revoking a credential, disabling a member, or changing access bumps the generation and the member's epoch, so a revoked cookie stops working within ~5 s while Home Base is up
The administrator flag is local to this host and excluded from any future export/sync
userStories.testStrategy: State-machine tests for every transition, including passphrase use while active by the administrator and by anyone else, and recovery → active; transactional last-administrator test; revocation while apps keep running; Home Base stopped (apps refuse after 120 s); a snapshot made writable or symlinked is refused; login-reassignment test; API authorization tests (no UI source assertions)

userStories.title: Suite passkey service
acceptanceCriteria: Served by Home Base on its own socket and mounted at /_sovereign/auth/ in every server block, so each hostname sets its own host-only cookie
Members enroll multiple credentials (label, kind, AAGUID, transports, created/last-used) and revoke them, per the assurance policy matrix

Kind (D15): 'hardware' only with 'packed' attestation whose chain verifies to a root pinned in sovereignAuth; Home Base refuses to classify anything as hardware when no roots are loaded (the library would otherwise skip chain checks); self-attestation or an unpinned chain ⇒ not hardware. Each credential records the root it verified against

Pinned roots are updated through sovereignAuth releases; removing a root (e.g. vendor compromise) demotes credentials that verified against it on the next snapshot, and an administrator left without an attested hardware key is told to enroll a new one

Ceremonies use RP ID = the tailnet domain (D17), userVerification required, no PRF. Each ceremony's expected origin is the single origin of the hostname that served it (from X-Forwarded-Host), never the whole published list; an assertion produced on a sibling hostname is refused, and its cookie or token is never valid elsewhere

Attestation is requested ('direct') only when enrolling an administrator hardware key; ordinary enrollment requests 'none', because with roots pinned an unpinned packed chain is rejected outright rather than downgraded

Successful checks set a __Host-sv_assurance cookie (Secure, Path=/, no Domain, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict): Ed25519-signed {sub (stable user ID), aud (hostname), sid, cred, kind, epoch, auth_time}. The __Host- prefix is required because sibling hostnames are same-site and can otherwise plant cookies (D20)

Every-time tokens are minted only from a fresh ceremony and bind {sub, household, aud app, action, resolved target, digest}. For Home Base plans the digest is of the frozen plan (e.g. restore resolves 'latest' to a named backup before the 401) and the retry runs exactly that frozen plan; for apps it covers the canonical request body plus the target the app resolved. 60-second expiry; consumed atomically in SQLite (one consumption across processes and restarts)

The shared helper (/_sovereign/auth/stepup.js) turns a 401 step_up_required into its own confirm tap (iOS gesture), the ceremony, and one retry of the identical request; it never retries a request that changed
Signing-key rotation keeps the previous public key in the snapshot for one session window; losing the key invalidates sessions only
Members can see their check status (which credential, how long ago)
userStories.testStrategy: Unit tests for classification, cookie and token rules; concurrent redemption from two processes, restart, changed body, changed target ('latest' moved during the ceremony), cross-app redemption, redemption socket timeout; Playwright virtual-authenticator flows; attestation tests (pinned root passes; no roots loaded, self-attestation, and a valid chain to an unpinned root are not hardware; root removal demotes); VM rehearsal with real 1Password, Apple Passwords, and a hardware key on macOS and iOS

userStories.title: Home Base admin on tailnet identity + passkeys
acceptanceCriteria: Home Base admin moves to svc:<instance>-homebase behind its nginx socket (D14); no TCP listener; :3080 is retired after a redirect period. Home Base also serves the nginx-only identity endpoint (D1) and the per-app redemption sockets (D19)

A route authorization matrix covers every Home Base route (reads and mutations: config, publishing, directory, roles, access, enrollment grants, recovery, plans) with its required level from the assurance policy; a test fails if a route is missing from it
Every mutation uses the mutation guard; authorization runs before any mutation or step-up prompt; this closes the unauthenticated config route (bugBase #150) if it is not fixed sooner
Admin unlock requires the administrator's identity plus a passkey (8h session bound to the stable user ID and hostname)
Administrator actions and privileged plans need an every-time attested hardware key, bound to the plan's digest
userStories.testStrategy: Route-matrix completeness test; API authorization tests per route; cross-site form and sibling-hostname request tests; VM rehearsal of setup, active, recovery, and reset

userStories.title: Pilot apps: one low-friction app and one sensitive canary
acceptanceCriteria: A previously passwordless Node app runs in tailnet mode: member auto-selected, picker and PINs replaced by role checks, kid and parent paths both exercised
The finance app runs as the sensitive canary on its own hostname and user: 30-day session, recent checks for linking accounts and exports, kid views at tailnet level (D7)
Apps link local member rows to suite_member_id once (administrator confirms each match); unlinked members see an 'ask the administrator' page
Local credentials stay intact and usable in local mode until after the feature's rollback window

userStories.testStrategy: App tests; browser tests with parent, kid, unknown login, and tagged host; hostile sibling-page test from svc:home against the canary

userStories.title: Rollout runbook and VM rehearsal
acceptanceCriteria: docs/suite-identity-rollout-runbook.md covers read-only pre-checks, tailnet policy and service definitions, dependency-ordered cutover and rollback, verification, and the tailnet-rename re-enrollment procedure

The rehearsal adds the one spike-3 check not yet run: a second tagged host trying to advertise an instance-qualified service the first host serves is refused by the Home Base guard (and is not auto-approved)
A full rehearsal on a test VM passes the spike-1, spike-2, and spike-3 checklists, an interrupted cutover, and a rollback, before any production host changes

followUpFeatures: App waves, each in its own app repo: wave 1 remaining low-friction apps (fasting, help desk, calendar, and whichever wasn't the pilot); wave 2 passphrase apps (home ops, photos, estate documents); wave 3 operator apps (trading, Bitcoin accounting) with the Python port of sovereignAuth
Estate-documents app: fix credential tier classification and iOS unlock guidance (tracked in bugBase)
Multi-host directory export/import, then peer pairing (decision D5 deferred)
Machine tokens for MCP/agents and publish-token apps (deferred)
OIDC sign-in for households without a tailnet identity provider (deferred; not part of the adapter until built)

high: Any remaining TCP path to nginx or an app makes identity headers forgeable; the planner must refuse tailnet mode unless the socket-only path is in place, on both deployment paths

Low-friction apps share one hostname and one service user, so a compromised one can act as any member who visits it within that hostname; accepted, because those apps hold no sensitive data and get no assurance cookies
Administrator lockout if all credentials are lost; recovery and reset must be rehearsed
Tailscale Services behavior (layer-7 identity headers, socket targets, X-Forwarded-For handling) is documented but unproven on our version; spike 3 gates SID-001
medium: Every request now depends on the Home Base identity endpoint; if Home Base is down, tailnet-mode apps see no identity until it returns (fail closed). Keep the endpoint small, cached per client IP for seconds, and separate from the admin process's heavy work
Each new hostname is an instance-qualified Tailscale Service that needs a tailnet policy entry and approval; more setup for other households
Renaming the tailnet invalidates every passkey (RP ID); the runbook's re-enrollment procedure is the only path
iOS requires a fresh user gesture for WebAuthn; the shared helper must keep its own confirm tap
Kids' surfaces must not regress; wave 1 must be invisible to kids except for removing the picker
If Home Base stops writing the snapshot, tailnet-mode apps refuse members once it ages out; max age must balance revocation speed against outages

Service hostnames are one browser site (D20): a compromised low-friction app can send credentialed requests and plant unprefixed cookies on sensitive hostnames. Mitigated by the exact-Origin, __Host-, aud, side-effect-free GET and resource-isolation rules; every new route needs those tests
low: Hardware vendors outside the pinned roots can't serve as administrator hardware keys until their root is added

preFlightChecklist: Spike 3 passed on the test VM (2026-10-25); confirm each production host runs Tailscale ≥ 1.102.4
Confirm on each production host (read-only): tailscale serve get-config --all, ss -ltnp, host tags, and how svc:home is defined
Confirm @simplewebauthn/server version alignment with the estate-documents app
Keep family names, real tailnet names, and private hostnames out of this repo's docs and tests
